12: > Use Unity's comprehensive sign-in solution that provides persistent accounts across games, devices, and platforms.
13: 
14: ## Overview
15: 
16: Unity Player Accounts is Unity's comprehensive sign-in solution that supports persistence across games, devices and platforms. It's an end-to-end account system that includes a user flow UX, email and password, social sign-in options, and data access and deletion flows.
17: 
18: Unity Player Accounts is an external identity provider which is natively integrated with Unity Gaming Services and the Authentication SDK. It has multiple benefits such as SSO, organization-level player pool, and cross-game, cross-device or cross-platform gameplay.
19: 
20: | Technical feature                                | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
21: | ------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
22: | Integrated with Unity Gaming Services and Editor | Player Accounts is the out-of-the-box sign-in and identity solution for Unity Gaming Services and Unity's ecosystem. It's seamlessly integrated with Authentication and offers additional features such as organization-level player identifiers.                                                                                                                     |
23: | Cross-platform and cross-device                  | Your players can sign up and sign into your games across a range of platforms, including iOS, Android, Windows, and macOS.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
24: | Cross-game                                       | Leverage organization-level player identifiers to maintain persistent player profiles across all of your games.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
25: | Streamlined user sign-up & sign-in journey       | Your players can sign up or sign in to their accounts using their preferred method, such as email and password or social accounts like Google or Apple.                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
26: | Integrate once and forget it                     | Our browser-based sign-up and sign-in flow is automatically updated with new features without any integration or update for your game. Focus on building and running your game, without the need to reintegrate your authentication solution. Once integrated, you can rely on Player Accounts to stay up to date with the latest security improvements and features. |
27: 
28: ## Get started
29: 
30: To get started you must first [install the Authentication package](./get-started.md), and then configure a Unity Player Accounts ID provider in the Unity Dashboard.
31: 
32: The C# methods required for interacting with Unity Player Accounts are included within the Authentication package in the dedicated `PlayerAccountService` namespace.
33: 
34: ### Set up the Unity Player Accounts ID provider
35: 
36: You can set up Unity Player Accounts directly in the Unity Dashboard.
37: 
38: 1. In the Unity Editor select **Services** > **Authentication** > **Configure** from the navigation menu.
39: 2. Select **Go to Dashboard** to open the Authentication Identity providers web page.
40: 3. On the web page, select **Add Identity Provider** and select **Unity Player Accounts**.
41: 4. Enter the provider details in the **Add Unity Player Accounts** dialog.
42:    > **Note:**
43:    >
44:    > For the sign-in flow to work in the Unity Editor Play mode, include the **PC** platform.
45: 5. Select **Add provider**.
46: 6. Return to **Services** > **Authentication** > **Configure** in the Unity Editor and select **Refresh**. This displays the **Unity Player Accounts** ID provider.
47: 7. In the Unity Editor, navigate to **Services** > **Unity Player Accounts** > **Configure** and ensure the Client ID is correctly set. This is also where you can optionally configure scopes and custom redirect URI schemes.
48: 
49: > **Note:**
50: >
51: > The authentication flow works without the need for configuring the redirect URI, as long as the registered URIs follow the prescribed format:
52: >
53: > * Desktop/Standalone: `http://localhost/callback`
54: > * Android/IOS default deep link URI: `unitydl://com.unityplayeraccounts.{unity-project-id}`
55: 
56: ### Before you publish your game
57: 
58: Review Unity's compliance and branding guidelines:
59: 
60: * You must provide a way for players to request data deletion and disclosure requests for your application and their Unity Player Account.
61: * Include a link to the Unity Player Accounts account deletion page: `https://player-account.unity.com/delete-account`
62: * Include a link to the Unity Player Accounts privacy support email for data disclosure or other privacy requests: `unity-player-login-privacy@unity3d.com`
63: * You must always ensure compliance with [Unity Terms of Service](https://unity.com/legal/terms-of-service).
64: * You must always maintain, display, and abide by a conspicuously placed Privacy Policy that makes appropriate disclosure to end-users, complies with all applicable privacy and data protection laws and regulations, and grants Unity the necessary rights required for the use of the Unity Player Accounts service.
65: 
66: ### Unity Player Accounts sample
67: 
68: The Authentication package includes a sample scene which is fully integrated with Unity Player Accounts. Use this sample to try out the flow after completing the configuration steps above.
69: 
70: To import the sample, follow these steps:
71: 
72: 1. In the Unity Editor, select **Window** > **Package Management**.
73: 2. Select the Authentication package.
74: 3. Select **Samples** > **Import**.
75: 
76: Open the sample scene under **Assets** > **Samples** > **Authentication** > \[Package-Version] > **UI Example** > **UnityPlayerAccountsUIExample**.
77: 
78: ## Sign in a returning player or create new player
79: 
80: Use the `PlayerAccountService.Instance.StartSignInAsync` method to start the player sign-in flow for Unity Player Accounts. This opens the system browser to `https://player-login.unity.com`, prompts the player to sign in, and then returns them to the application with their Unity Player Accounts credentials.
81: 
82: When they have signed in to Unity Player Accounts and returned to your application with their credentials, use the `AuthenticationService.Instance.SignInWithUnityAsync` method to either:
83: 
84: * Create a new Unity Authentication player with the Unity Player Accounts credentials.
85: * Sign in an existing player using the Unity Player Accounts credentials.
86: 
87: The `PlayerAccountService.Instance.SignedIn` event will let us know when the browser-based Unity Player Accounts sign in has succeeded and we can proceed with signing in to Unity Authentication.
88: 
89: The credentials required to sign in to Unity Authentication are the access token available on `PlayerAccountService.Instance.AccessToken`.
90: 
91: ```cs
92: async void Start()
93: {
94:     await UnityServices.InitializeAsync();
95: 
96:     // Register the Unity Player Accounts sign-in event handler after services initialization.
97:     PlayerAccountService.Instance.SignedIn += SignInWithUnityAuth;
98: }
99: 
100: // Call this from a button or other application-specific trigger to begin the sign-in flow.
101: async void StartPlayerAccountsSignInAsync()

10: # Manage linked external identities
11: 
12: > Handle account linking conflicts and manage multiple linked external identities for players.
13: 
14: Managing a player’s linked external identities is important to ensure your players can secure their accounts and use the access method of their choice. When offering account linking to your customers, it's important to properly handle every scenario.
15: 
16: A player can have multiple linked unique external identities (e.g. Apple, Facebook, Google). However, an external identity can only be linked to a single player (e.g. one player ID cannot be linked to multiple Google identities).
17: 
18: ### Retrieve a player's information
19: 
20: `GetPlayerInfoAsync()` can be used to load a player’s information which includes their linked identities.
21: 
22: ### Handle account linking conflicts
23: 
24: The linking operations will throw an error if an identity is already linked to another player.
25: 
26: When there’s a conflict, it’s important to inform the player of the situation.
27: 
28: An optional parameter can be provided to force the link to be created. Using this option will remove the initial link which can make the initial account unrecoverable.
29: 
30: We recommend offering the following options in case of conflict:
31: 
32: * Choose to force the link and keep the current account.
33: * Choose to switch to the initial account by using the `SignInWith*` API.
34: * Choose to cancel the action and remain in the current state.
35: 
36: 
37: **Frame:**
38: ![An example workflow for identity management that presents the previously mentioned options for how to handle conflicts. ](/api/media?file=/authentication/media/images/identity-management.png)

2: UID2 overview
3: Unified ID 2.0 overview
4: UID2 is a framework that enables deterministic identity for advertising opportunities on the open internet for many
5: participants
6: across the advertising ecosystem. The UID2 framework enables publisher websites, mobile apps, and Connected TV (CTV) apps to monetize through programmatic workflows. Built as an open-source, standalone solution with its own unique namespace, the framework offers privacy controls designed to help participants meet local market requirements.
7: note
8: The term "UID2" can refer to either the framework or an actual identifier. Unless otherwise indicated, this page provides an overview of the UID2 framework.
9: Guiding principles
10: ​
11: The UID2 framework has the following principles as its foundation:
12: First-party relationships
13: : UID2 enables advertisers to activate their first-party data on publisher websites across the open internet.
14: Non-proprietary (universal) standard
15: : All
16: participants
17: in the advertising ecosystem who execute an appropriate participation agreement can access UID2.
18: Open source
19: : The source code for the
20: UID2 component services
21: is publicly available.
22: Interoperable
23: : The framework allows other identity solutions (commercial and proprietary) to integrate and provide UID2 tokens with their offerings.
24: Secure and encrypted data
25: : UID2 leverages multiple layers of security to help protect user and other participant data.
26: Consumer control
27: : Consumers can opt out of UID2 at any time through the
28: Transparency and Control Portal
29: .
30: Technical design principles
31: ​
32: The UID2 framework is built on the following technical principles:
33: Distributed integration
34: : Multiple certified integration paths provide options for publishers, advertisers, and third-party data providers to manage and exchange UID2 tokens.
35: Decentralized storage
36: : The framework does not have centralized storage for personal data (
37: DII
38: ) mappings. All participants maintain only their own data.
39: Lean infrastructure
40: : The UID2 system is light and inexpensive to operate.
41: Internet scale
42: : The UID2 infrastructure can scale to address the continuously increasing needs of
43: participants
44: and to meet the performance demands of specific geographic regions.
45: Self-reliant
46: : UID2 does not rely on external services for the processing of real-time bidding (RTB) data.

54: How does Axon AI work?
55: Businesses of all sizes use AppLovin Ads to automate, optimize, and manage their marketing efforts.
56: Advertisers set specific return goals for their advertising campaigns.
57: Axon AI’s predictive algorithms then evaluate potential impressions with the goals of meeting advertisers’ return on advertising spend targets and other marketing objectives and finding the users most likely to download or otherwise engage with their product(s).
58: AppLovin bids on impressions based on Axon AI’s determination of the value of the impression to the particular advertiser.
59: AppLovin earns revenues based on the value we drive for advertisers.  Our performance-based advertising model therefore demands that ads served by us lead to genuine, high-intent engagement, ensuring our campaigns deliver meaningful, measurable results for advertisers.
60: What data does Axon AI use?
61: Complex AI models, like Axon AI, train and optimize on a continual basis using an assortment of data.  Our models use device and network information and other information we have collected, or our partners share, about users’ engagement with applications, ads, and other digital properties, as described in our
62: Privacy Policy
63: and
64: How AppLovin Shows You Ads
65: page.  In addition, our models use win or loss notifications from our in-app bidding and monetization solution known as AppLovin Max, which all bidders receive depending on whether the bidder won or lost a particular impression.  Our models also use advertisers’ own data about their users if they choose to share that data with us.
66: We do not collect or seek to elicit—and our models do not ingest—users’ “sensitive personal information” (such as social security numbers, precise geolocation, racial and ethnic characteristics, religious or philosophical beliefs, or the contents of messages) or protected characteristics (such as age and gender).  In addition, we do not collect or seek to elicit—and our models do not ingest—other bidders’ bid information or other bidders’ user data.  We also explicitly prohibit partners from initializing our technologies in connection with “children” or otherwise providing us with children’s data, and we prohibit apps exclusively designed for and/or exclusively directed to children on our platform.
67: For more information, please review our
68: Privacy Policy
69: and
70: How AppLovin Shows You Ads
71: page.
72: How does Axon AI continue to improve?
73: On an ongoing basis, Axon AI’s models experience compounding improvements through self-learning, continuing data ingestion, and engineering oversight and enhancements.  As more advertisers use our performance-based advertising solutions, the models improve through additional data and better insights (per the collection described above), which then further enhances the efficiency and effectiveness of AppLovin Ads.

31: The power of Axon 2
32: For most of our history, AppLovin focused primarily on games. That was not a strategic limitation; it was a choice to stay focused while we built our technical capabilities. We became experts in helping game developers grow their businesses, and that focus, paired with technology, helped us become the largest user acquisition channel for mobile gaming in the world.
33: However, accurately valuing consumers playing games for offers that aren’t games requires predicting an even more complex chain of behaviors. We have to predict ad engagement, click-through rates, app or site engagement, conversion likelihood, payment probability, purchase size, and repeat behavior over time outside of the contextual relevancy of games. Advertisers require AppLovin to give them a return. If they spend $1,000, they must generate meaningfully more than $1,000 in lifetime value. Even small inaccuracies in prediction break the economics.
34: In April 2023, we rolled out our AI model, Axon 2. While Axon 1 performed this task well for gaming, Axon 2 significantly expanded our model capacity in gaming and unlocked every other major advertiser category. 208: How Unity’s D28 IAP ROAS optimizer prevents D7 cannibalization
209: The question remains that if both campaign types bid on impressions in the same inventory, won’t they compete against each other and drive up costs?
210: Unity's analysis of D28 converters reveals that only 38%* of users who convert with in-app purchases by D28 spend in the first week. In other words, roughly two-thirds of high-value D28 spenders showed no early IAP conversion signals whatsoever.
211: These aren’t players who nearly converted on D7 but needed a few more days. They’re a different player cohort with different motivations, engagement patterns, and conversion triggers.
212: This is where Unity Vector's support is vital. Traditional optimization models can only see what happens after a user installs: Did they convert? How much did they spend? Unity Vector enables Unity IAP ROAS optimizers to see something more.
213: Because Unity powers both game creation and user growth, Unity Vector has unique visibility into player behavior and patterns.
214: Unity Vector combines holistic player and game intelligence to understand why certain players match with certain games, and when they're likely to convert. It uses both attributed data and unattributed data, like cross-game behavioral patterns and aggregate cohort insights, to distinguish between these player types at the moment of bid decision.
215: The future of ROAS optimization with Unity Vector
216: When UA efficiency increasingly plays a large role in which games succeed and which fail, leaving only 38% of IAP converters addressed isn't viable. And without the early converters of D7 campaigns, optimizers have less signals and businesses have less to invest in their late-game campaigns.
217: Both are necessary. And with Unity Vector powering both optimization windows, these Unity Ads campaign types can deliver better results as the model learns from Unity's place at the intersection of game creation and growth.
218: The architectural decision to optimize for holistic player and game intelligence means Unity Vector's optimization capabilities improve alongside games as they evolve and player behaviors shift - allowing Unity Vector to provide later LTV predictions as the market demands increasingly longer optimization windows. Ultimately, this ensures Unity is able to help creators build games that players love to play, and turn those games into profitable, sustainable businesses.
